title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6989 – Reuters estimate
body: The fixing mechanism matters most right now because of what it has been signalling over recent weeks. The PBOC set its reference rate at the widest weak side deviation from market estimates in six months in late August, after the yuan touched a three and a half year high, a clear sign of discomfort with the pace of gains rather than the level itself. Traders should read this as the central bank applying the brakes rather than attempting to reverse the broader trend, since the yuan has still risen a meaningful amount against the dollar this year. The balancing act Beijing faces is straightforward: a stronger currency helps with capital stability and import costs, but too rapid a rise risks eroding export competitiveness at a time when the domestic economy is showing renewed signs of softness. Watching the gap between the daily fixing and consensus estimates remains one of the more reliable ways to gauge PBOC intent in the days ahead.---The daily fixing is Beijing's quietest but clearest tool for telling markets how fast it wants the yuan to move, and lately the message has been to slow down.Summary: The PBOC sets the daily USD/CNY reference rate, or midpoint, at around 0115 GMT, one of the most closely watched signals in Asian FX markets. An administrator introduces a supposedly exclusive brokerage app, perhaps claiming access to special allocations or an AI trading service. You deposit a small amount. The app shows a profit, and you may even receive a small withdrawal. Encouraged, you deposit more. When you try to withdraw a larger sum, you are told to pay a tax, security deposit or account-unlocking fee first. The crucial lesson: several apparently reassuring experiences can all come from the same source. The group members, adviser, app and customer support may be controlled by the same operation.

title: Palm Oil Rebounds After Recent Weakness
body: Malaysian palm oil futures firmed, stabilizing above MYR 4,850 per tonne and breaking a recent losing streak. The market drew support from stronger soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade and higher crude oil prices, amid ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Expectations of tighter global supply further underpinned prices. Indonesia's B50 biodiesel mandate is set to channel more palm oil into domestic consumption, while El Niño-related weather risks could constrain production in both Indonesia and Malaysia. Demand prospects also improved. Palm oil imports by India, the world's largest buyer, increased 7% from July to 782,761 tonnes in August, the highest level since February, as refiners replenished inventories ahead of the festival season. On the policy front, Malaysia raised its crude palm oil reference price for October but maintained the export duty at 10%. However, upside momentum was limited by weakness on the Dalian exchanges and evidence of softer export demand. Cargo surveyor data showed that Malaysian palm oil product shipments declined by an estimated 12.8%–24.7% month-on-month during September 1–20. title: South Korean Won Rebounds
body: The South Korean won firmed to around 1,360 per dollar, rebounding from four-week lows as oil prices fell sharply. WTI crude dropped 4.5% to below $100 a barrel, while Brent declined more than 3%, amid hopes for progress in US-Iran negotiations and signs of recovery in Saudi oil shipments. The US 10-year Treasury yield also slipped back below 5% after hitting recent highs last week, easing support for the dollar. At the same time, South Korea's robust export performance continued to support the won. Exports surged 78% year-on-year in the first 20 days of September, driven by a 259% increase in semiconductor shipments, which helped boost dollar inflows. Still, the dollar remained relatively firm as investors monitored the prospect of another Federal Reserve rate hike later this year. Separately, the Bank of Korea reiterated that it will weigh inflation, growth, and financial stability in determining the timing and pace of any further interest rate increases. title: Indonesian Shares Drop for 3rd Session
body: Indonesia's IDX Composite slipped 30 points, or 0.4%, to 6,354 in Tuesday morning trade, extending losses into a third session as investors stayed cautious ahead of Bank Indonesia's policy decision. The central bank opened its two-day meeting today amid renewed pressure on the rupiah and persistent inflationary risks. At the same time, lawmakers continued debating revisions to the 2003 fiscal law that could permit a higher budget deficit to finance social and welfare programs. Finance Minister Suahasil Nazara emphasized that any discussion of changes to the statutory deficit ceiling of 3% of GDP should be conducted constructively. Losses on the local bourse were partly limited by robust gains on Wall Street overnight, supported by optimism over Meta Platforms' new AI agent. title: Copper Extends Rally to Sixth Session
body: Copper futures climbed above $6.70 per pound on Tuesday, extending their winning streak to a sixth consecutive session as persistent supply concerns continued to underpin prices. According to Sprott Asset Management, global mined copper production could decline this year for the first time since 2017—despite record price levels—owing to operational disruptions, deteriorating ore grades, and subdued output from Chile. Global mine production fell 1.1% year over year in the first half of 2026, while issues at major operations in Indonesia and the Democratic Republic of Congo have removed an estimated 600,000 tonnes from anticipated annual supply. Meanwhile, demand remains robust, driven by power grid expansion, AI data center construction, and defense-related uses. Traders are also closely monitoring prospective US tariffs on copper. The Commerce Department has proposed duties of 15% starting in January 2027, rising to 30% from 2028 onward, subject to a final decision by the president. title: Taiwan Equities Hit New High, Top 48,000 Mark
body: The TAIEX, Taiwan's benchmark stock index, climbed 692 points, or 1.5%, to 48,411 in Tuesday morning trading, extending its winning streak to a fifth consecutive session and setting a new record high. The rally was driven primarily by electronic technology shares. The index crossed the 48,000 threshold for the first time on June 23, 2026, when it touched an intraday peak of 48,219 before retreating. On Tuesday, the electronic technology subindex advanced 1.8%. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) — the world's largest contract chipmaker and accounting for more than 40% of the market's total capitalization — edged up 0.6%. Other major tech names posted stronger gains: MediaTek and ASE Technology Holding jumped 8.6% and 6.3%, respectively. United Microelectronics surged 6.1%, while Unimicron Technology Corp. rallied 9.8%. The broader market followed Wall Street higher, supported by robust demand for AI-related stocks, while easing oil prices and lower US Treasury yields provided additional support. Sentiment was further boosted by optimism ahead of this week's Trump–Xi summit, where discussions are expected to focus on AI and tariffs. title: Corn Holds Near 3-Year Peak
body: Corn futures remained above $5.40 per bushel after reaching their highest level since July 2023, supported by robust US export demand, tightening global supplies, and expectations of increased agricultural trade with China. US corn export inspections rose 40% year-on-year to 1.94 million tonnes in the week ended September 17, surpassing market expectations and pushing 2026/27 shipments further ahead of last year's pace. In the Midwest, heavy rainfall is delaying harvest in some areas and constraining the near-term flow of new supply, although overall progress remains slightly ahead of the five-year average. Global fundamentals also remain supportive: the USDA projects a nearly 30-million-tonne gap between world corn production and consumption in 2026/27, the largest deficit in more than three decades. Traders are closely monitoring this week's Trump–Xi meeting for signs of progress on US agricultural purchases, while ongoing disruptions to Black Sea grain exports continue to lend additional support to prices. title: Platinum Futures Rangebound
body: Platinum futures hovered near $1,800 an ounce, trading within a narrow range as a stronger US dollar offset easing inflation pressures stemming from falling oil prices. Crude benchmarks extended their decline amid signs of intensified diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict in the Middle East and restore regional energy flows. This helped temper inflation concerns and reduced expectations for additional interest rate hikes, thereby lowering the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets such as platinum. Still, hawkish remarks from Federal Reserve officials reinforced expectations for a more restrictive US interest-rate path following last week's first rate increase in three years. From a fundamental perspective, the backdrop remained broadly supportive. The WPIC projects a 5% rise in industrial platinum demand in 2026, partly underpinned by investment in AI-related infrastructure, even as automotive demand is forecast to decline by 4%. Although the market is expected to post a surplus of around 265,000 ounces in 2026, the WPIC anticipates that above-ground stocks will remain relatively tight, at the equivalent of only about 3.4 months of global demand, following the substantial deficits recorded in previous years. title: Bitcoin Hovers Near 8-Month High
body: Bitcoin held above $85,000 on Tuesday, trading near its highest level since January. The cryptocurrency has retained a gain of roughly 7% over the past five days and about 35% over the past three months. The recent advance has been partly driven by softer crude oil prices and renewed institutional interest. US spot Bitcoin ETFs registered net inflows of $433 million on September 18, while corporate demand also picked up as Strategy resumed Bitcoin purchases following a three-week hiatus. title: Heating Oil Retreats Further
body: US heating oil prices fell below $4.90 per gallon, extending their pullback from last week's record high as improved tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and renewed diplomatic efforts eased immediate supply fears. Satellite data indicated a sharp increase in Saudi oil loadings in the Persian Gulf, signaling that exports have been redirected back through the Strait of Hormuz while the East–West pipeline remains offline. Reports suggest that the pipeline could partially resume operations within days. Even so, seasonal dynamics point to renewed upward pressure. With winter approaching, heating demand is likely to rise, while ongoing refinery maintenance could limit output and tighten already constrained supplies. According to EIA data, distillate inventories—including diesel and heating oil—were 13% below their five-year average in the week ending September 11. At the same time, Russia intends to extend diesel export restrictions through October, and Ukrainian strikes have disrupted production at key refineries, further constricting global distillate availability.
